issues.legal_issue: A village grant is not confirmed as a whole when the confirming authority recognizes only part of the village and leaves the remaining area unconfirmed despite its being available for confirmation.
material_facts: The claimed grant concerned a village treated as having been granted in Inam.
At the settlement, one half of the village was possessed by a zamindar and treated in the accounts as part of the zamindari; the other half was held by persons claiming through the Inam grantees.
The Inam Commissioner confirmed only the half held by the claimants and fixed a quit rent on it.
The remaining half was not confirmed, and there was nothing preventing the Commissioner from considering it for confirmation.
The State appealed a decision that the village was not an estate under the relevant statutory definition.
issues.conclusion: The confirmation of only part of the village did not establish that the grant of the village had been confirmed as a whole; the confirmed lands therefore did not constitute an estate under Section 3(2)(d), and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(2)(d) of the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, confirmation of a village grant requires recognition of the area covered by the grant. The entire grant must be confirmed, whether through one title deed or several; separate title deeds do not prevent the village from qualifying if they collectively recognize the entire grant. But recognition of only part does not confirm the entire grant where the remaining area was available for confirmation. The Court agreed with the approach in Srinivasa Ayyangar v. State of Madras and the formula in Somasundaram v. State of Madras, and distinguished cases such as Viswanadham Bros. v. Subbaiya and Bhavanarayana v. Merugu Venkatadu insofar as they concerned confirmation of the entire grant or did not involve partial confirmation. The Court also held Nistala Seshayya Bhukta v. Vasu Bageyya inapplicable because it concerned a statutory explanation not at issue in this case.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_village_estate_status and original_grant_claimed_to_cover_entire_village and only_part_of_original_grant_confirmed and remaining_area_available_for_confirmation

predicates.appeal_concerning_village_estate_status: A party appealed a decision determining whether a village grant met the legal test for estate status.
predicates.original_grant_claimed_to_cover_entire_v: The asserted original grant was a grant of the village as a whole.
predicates.only_part_of_original_grant_confirmed: The confirming authority recognized the grant in respect of only part of the area originally claimed.
predicates.remaining_area_available_for_confirmatio: The area left unconfirmed was available for consideration by the confirming authority.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning village estate status involves an asserted whole-village grant, only part of which was confirmed while the rest was available for confirmation, the village grant is not treated as an estate.
